name: Brazil (SPA/MF) Market Profile

regulator.name: Secretaria de Premios e Apostas (SPA), Ministerio da Fazenda
regulator.notes: Created by Decreto 11.907/2024. Filing portal: SIGAP, https://sigap.fazenda.gov.br

bindingStandards.name: Law 14.790/2023
bindingStandards.notes: Legalised fixed-odds betting AND online casino games including slots at federal level. Regulated market launched 2025-01-01. Only SPA-authorised operators are lawful.

bindingStandards.name: Portaria SPA/MF nº 722/2024 and the December 2024 amending ordinance (technical and data-centre requirements)
Portaria SPA/MF nº 300/2024 (recognition of certifying entities)
SPA online-gaming technical ordinance of August 2024
bindingStandards.notes: Exact ordinance number UNVERIFIED; this is the instrument understood to carry the RTP rule.

otherProhibitions.item: Government preparing to ban Fortune Tiger-style games ahead of the October 2026 election
otherProhibitions.notes: A theme and game-family level ban, not a mechanic ban. Monitor: this could remove an entire product category from the market.

minimum.source: SPA online-gaming technical ordinance, August 2024 (via multiple law firm and industry sources)
minimum.notes: Theoretical RTP per game over its expected life cycle. Well corroborated across independent secondary sources but NOT read from the official text. Additional rule: the advertised top prize must be winnable at least once per 100 MILLION plays - this is a maximum-prize probability floor, which constrains extreme long-tail jackpot design and must be computed explicitly in the PAR sheet.

socialProgrammeRestriction.value: Government preparing to block betting access for Bolsa Familia and BPC benefit recipients
socialProgrammeRestriction.notes: If enacted this becomes a player-eligibility check against a government dataset, an integration requirement.

requirement.value: STRICT. The betting system must run and its data be stored in data centres LOCATED IN BRAZILIAN TERRITORY. The only exception is a country holding an international judicial-cooperation agreement with Brazil in BOTH civil and criminal matters and complying with Brazilian data protection law.
requirement.source: Portaria SPA/MF nº 722/2024 plus the December 2024 amending ordinance
requirement.notes: One of the strictest data residency regimes in this dataset. Determines deployment topology and must be settled in phase 1 of market entry assessment.

localEntityRequirement.value: Brazilian legal entity required, with a Brazilian partner holding at least 20%, and a mandatory .bet.br domain
localEntityRequirement.notes: The 20% local shareholding is a corporate structuring requirement, not a technical one, but it materially affects market entry feasibility and timeline.

certification.labModel: Mandatory. The betting system, the sports-betting server and the REMOTE GAMING (slots) SERVER must each be certified by an SPA-recognised certifying entity, filed in Portuguese via SIGAP.
certification.notes: Accreditation regime under Portaria SPA/MF nº 300/2024. Six accredited certifiers as of January 2025, confirmed to include GLI and eCOGRA. Trisigma was authorised in November 2024 (Portaria SPA/MF nº 1.775) and its authorisation was REVOKED in November 2025 - verify a certifier's current standing before engaging. Full current list UNVERIFIED. Note also that filings must be in Portuguese, which adds translation lead time for technical documentation.

consultantNotes: Brazil is the largest newly regulated slot market in this dataset. The binding constraints are less about game mechanics and more about STRUCTURE: in-country data centres, a Brazilian entity with a 20% local partner, a .bet.br domain, Portuguese-language certification filings, and a specific accredited certifier.

The 'top prize winnable at least once per 100 million plays' rule is a maximum-prize PROBABILITY floor. It is a genuine maths model constraint, and it is the mirror image of Germany's requirement to disclose the maximum-prize probability. Both require the same computation.

Framework volatility is high: an advertising ordinance, a reopened authorisation consultation, a possible game-family ban and a constitutional challenge are all live in 2026. Do not treat a Brazilian licence as a stable baseline.
